  in the full numbering, and administrators are shown each case under
  Configuration → Split editions. The row names the tests and the drive.

- **O191 — a work an account sees part of. Closed 2026-11-04.** What
  remained after decision 4 was the truth and notes routes sending, and truth
  replacing, the entries of an edition the account cannot see. They now send
  nothing of it, and a write keeps it as stored; a narrowed edition is held to
  the same rule. The row names the tests.

- **O240 — a notes write retried after a 412 kept the numbering it read.
  Closed.** The web reader sends each note's and each position's page beside
  its slot, and the server places a write by that page, so a write read
  before a renumbering, a 412's retry among them, lands on the page it was
  made on, and no reload follows a 412, as decision 11 ruled. An untouched
  note is kept as it is, and a page a stamp moved is forwarded to the
  archive's new digest. A note naming a page the account is not sent, or a
  note whose page is gone that another device has since moved, is refused
  in a sentence that says to reload. A position's missing validator is
  answered by its page, not by a tag.

- **O241 — a limited account's labeller was offered a narrowed edition.
  Closed, by consequence of O58.** Only an administrator writes a truth
  document, and the labeller is drawn for an administrator alone; an
  administrator is never narrowed, so no labeller is offered a narrowed
  edition, and the server stores the document an administrator sends whole.

- **O242 — a hand value carried during a removal misses an existing
  document. Open.** The removal's own pass folds under `Documents::Skip`,
  which writes no file, and the pass after the commit has nothing left to
  fold, so a target that already has a document keeps the old one and is
  reported stale. The database keeps the value, and the row names one fix.
- **O243 — a work left holding a file another work holds is never folded
  into it. Open.** Removing the older directory of a volume split per file
  leaves its work standing beside the work its copy now sits in, reported
  unfolded on every derive, as the user ruled on 2026-11-04. An old edition
  that is part of the new work's members but not a run of them is refused the
  same way, and one beside an edition the derive still writes is never
  offered to the fold at all and is reported only as a kept edition; the
  ruling is applied to both. Folding them needs an edition placed member by
  member in a larger one, a written work's stale edition superseded, rows
  numbered by slot moved with their members, and a rule for a row that names
  no page.
- **O244 — a removal left positions and notes in the old numbering.
  Closed.** Deleting a work's earlier members moved every slot after them
  onto a later page, or past the end. Lane 2 of the pre-deploy design gives
  each position and note an anchor beside its slot, the page it was written
  on. Every position written through `state::` fills it, as does every new
  or moved note, and every read resolves it, so the row stays on its page,
  unless an earlier copy of its archive in the same edition goes: the copies
  renumber, and the row resolves on a later copy's page or as a lost file
  (the spec's decision 11). The fold's writes keep a row's anchor as it is.
  A position whose page is gone opens at its stored slot, clamped, and a
  note there is kept and marked `stale`; neither is rewritten. A stamp,
  which gives an archive a new digest and keeps its pages, moves each
  anchor on a member of a stamped edition to that member's new digest and
  occurrence, so where an edition lists one archive twice each copy keeps
  its own rows. A derive before the next scan of a stamped archive's
  directory writes the old digest back onto its member from the scan's
  record; O270 records what the rows read until that scan and after it.
  *O270 has since closed, on 2026-11-17 — see its entry below.*
  Go-public lane 4 did what remained: a removal, rehearsed or real, counts
  the anchored positions and notes on works it keeps whose page it takes,
  and both Remove dialogs say so; a note whose page is gone is drawn as such
  in the note panel. A row with no anchor, written before the anchors
  existed and not anchored since (a position by `state::put_progress_at`, a
  note by a notes write that moves it), answers its stored slot, so a
  removal can still move it to another page, and does not count it.
  `page_flag`, `run` and `truth_page` are keyed by page and are not
  anchored.
- **O245 — Move's refusal named a scan or a rule save while another job held
  the store's lock. Closed.** Every refusal for that lock now says "a scan or
  another library job is running; … once it has finished": Move's, Remove
  from this library's, the rule save's and the stamp's, by the user's ruling
  of 2026-11-08, so none names a cause that is not there. The row named the
  refusal Move and Remove from this library share; its survey found the rule
  save's own refusal, which named a scan or a save, to be the same defect,
  and the stamp's "currently running against this library" went by the same
  ruling. Each of the four is asserted whole, written out in its test. The
  overlapping-libraries PR 1's pre-merge claim check found it, and found the
  same sentence on the same arm on `main` 6067071d, so it is older than that
  branch. The spec's decision 18 still lists four holders of the lock; it is
  a design record and is left as written.
- **O122 — `work.sidecar()` waits on the work's lock on the async worker.
  Open, and widened.** PR 1 builds an account's view of a work on the async
  worker, in `view::of_work` and `view::of_edition`, so the wait `main` had
  in six handlers now comes in every handler that takes its view from them:
  `routes::get_sidecar`, `get_notes`, `put_notes`, `get_truth`, `put_truth`,
  `get_progress`, `put_progress` and `opds::work_feed` through
  `view::of_work`, and `routes::get_page`, `get_thumb`, `opds::stream_page`,
  `opds::cover`, `download::edition` and `download::member` through
  `view::of_edition`; `opds::works` has it too. On `main`, `put_notes`,
  `put_progress`, both downloads, `opds::cover` and `get_thumb`'s tiles took
  that read inside their own `spawn_blocking`. The user ruled on 2026-11-04 to
  record it in the row; the fix is to build the view on the blocking pool.

**The overlapping-libraries PR 2**, a directory nested inside another
library's, closed O204, opened O246, O247, O248, O249 and O250, and added
to the rows of O47, O81, O238 and O244.

- **O204 — the add compared the stored roots before its transaction.
  Closed 2026-11-04.** Both ways of adding a directory now compare it with
  the stored roots inside the transaction that inserts it, and read the disk
  before it. The row names the test.
- **O246 — a directory at or inside a folder read as one volume is refused
  only once a derive has recorded the folder. Open.** Added before the outer
  directory's first derive, at the volume folder it left the volume in no
  work, and at a chapter folder inside it the outer's member counted fewer
  pages than the reader serves. The row says what is left to decide.
- **O247 — a hand-back leaves a document it cannot move where nothing
  reports it. Closed.** A removal now lists in its report's
  `orphan_documents`, with its title, each hand document of a surviving
  work that it leaves in a `.taiyaku` no directory holds any more; one left
  under a directory that stays is that directory's to read. The carry also
  follows works the hand-back does not move, a re-pointed work by the user's
  ruling of 2026-11-08 and one spanning two directories as the same defect
  by another path: every surviving work with a member under the removed
  directory is noted before any of its
  members goes or is re-pointed, so a work re-pointed at another directory's
  copy, or one spanning two directories, has its document carried or listed.
  A work the removal deletes keeps its document in place, unlisted, as on
  `main`. What remains: the rehearsal does not predict the documents left
  behind, the bare rename error has no test seam, and a re-pointed work that
  O243's fold later absorbs is listed with no `absorbed_into`, by reading.
  The Remove dialogs said the files on disk were untouched; O256 recorded
  it, and closed on 2026-11-09.
- **O248 — Move's lists of who gains and loses sight asked only about the
  moved directory. Closed.** A move and a Remove from this library compare
  each limited account's sight of the directory and of every directory
  nested in it, read once before the write, so an account that keeps the
  directory through a library around it and loses or gains one nested in it
  is named, and the dialogs say "sight of it or a directory inside it". The
  row's three-level case is the tests' fixture.
- **O249 — a directory removed while a scan derives can leave members with
  no directory. Open.** The removal goes ahead during any scan that does not
  touch the directory, the derive counts each member it meets in
  `root_removed_mid_derive`, and a later scan recovers it. The user ruled to
  record it rather than hold Remove… during every scan; it holds on `main`
  too.
- **O250 — a page held Remove… or Move… with nothing on it saying why.
  Closed.** A button held by something other than its directory's own scan
  now says why beside it, in its row's help or, for Move…, in a line under
  the directory's header, and is described by those words. The words are
  generic, by the user's ruling of 2026-11-09, since the status names no
  holder. The row had left out Remove from this library, held the same way,
  and Move…'s hold includes the job lock, which a scan of any library takes.
  O257 records a hold by the directory's own scan that nothing names. *O257
  has since closed, on 2026-11-16 — see its entry below.*

**O251 was opened and closed on 2026-11-05**, by the ruling that the PR 2
drive's download name be fixed on its own, and its bullet follows.

- **O251 — a download's name lost a leading `[`. Closed.** The strip that keeps
  a leading `-` off a filename took every leading character that was not a
  letter or digit, so a bracketed series lost its `[` and kept its `]`, and
  `(C99) Title` lost its `(`. It now takes `-`, `.` and whitespace only, and
  everything else stays, as the row says. A stem that opens with a zero-width
  or other invisible format character now keeps that too, as such a
  character elsewhere in the name already did.

**The overlapping-libraries PR 3**, the same directory in several libraries,
closed none, opened O252, O253 and O254 from its whole-branch review and
O255 from its drive, and added to the rows of O47, O225, O245 and O248:
`scan --add` of a held directory into another library now links it, O225
records the Filmstrip failures of 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-05, which a rerun no
longer always cleared, O245's refusal is now Remove from this library's too,
and Remove from this library shares Move's blind spot for directories nested
in the one it takes.

- **O252 — a library's page drew the other libraries' view of a directory as
  it last read it. Closed.** An unlink, a removal, a move or a New library
  now rewrites the lines other directories draw for the directory it wrote,
  the "No such …" pages say the list may be out of date, and a 409 in
  Move…'s or Remove…'s dialog has the page read the hold and the directory
  take up its own scan. A dialog drawing a refusal stays open, by the user's
  ruling of 2026-11-09; a removal's, refused for a hold, drops its counts
  and its confirm, as a refused move's drops its rehearsal and its confirm,
  and a moved directory is still no row in its target until the list is
  read, by other rulings that day.
- **O253 — the held Last scan width was held for a scanned table only.
  Closed.** Every row the page draws as scanning holds, from then, the
  width of the widest time ending failed and ending refused, so the column
  widens, if at all, as the scan starts, and no end of that scan moves it;
  the width lasts until the page is left, by the user's rulings of
  2026-11-09. A scan the page never drew as scanning, from the scheduler,
  another tab or the CLI, still moves the column when the list is next
  read. The table is `LibraryPage.tsx`'s, not `LibraryTable.tsx`'s as the
  row said.
- **O254 — a scan's line can name the wrong library. Closed.** The status
  names a scan's library only while that library reaches the directory, by
  reach and not links, as decision 20 asks, and sends its id beside its name,
  which the page compares, so a rename leaves the page's own scan its own.
  The one filter covers every way the state arises, which the survey found
  wider than the row: the `[only]` fallback, Scan library's own two steps, a
  library's removal and a `patch_root` that changes reach. An add's answer
  reads a linked directory's scan status inside the add, and New library
  answers 409, not 500, for a library removed before its answer. What
  remains is the window between the status's own two reads, one poll long:
  a move or a change of reach inside it is seen at the next poll, and a
  library removed inside it joins the null group through a names filter,
  which a test reaches by holding the status between the two reads.
- **O255 — a library's page kept its report line through a later add.
  Closed.** By the user's ruling of 2026-11-09, any write answered on a
  library's page takes away the line drawn there: an add, a rename, which no
  longer carries it to the new address, and a press of Scan library. By a
  later ruling that day they take away a line on the page of a directory
  open beside it too. An add's answer that takes away a line holding focus
  puts focus on Add directory….

**The PR that closed O245, O247 and O254 on 2026-11-08** opened O256, from
O247's survey, and its bullet follows.

- **O256 — the Remove dialogs said the files on disk were untouched. Closed.**
  They now say no archive on disk is changed, that a work that stays takes
  its documents to the directory that now holds its files if that directory
  keeps documents, and that the report after the removal lists any left
  behind as orphaned documents, by the user's rulings of 2026-11-09. The row
  overstated the move: a document goes only where the receiving directory
  keeps documents.

**The web PR that closed O250, O252, O253, O255 and O256 on 2026-11-09**
opened O257, from its Task 3 review, O258, from its whole-branch review,
O259 and O260, from its drive, and O261, from the reviews of its first two
tasks, and narrowed O202, whose dialogs no status read closes under their
write any more, and whose removal refused for a hold leaves no counts and
no confirm under its refusal; the bullets of O257 to O261 follow.

- **O257 — a directory's own scan, named beside a sibling's, holds Scan
  directory and Remove… with no "Scanning…". Closed.** `RootRow` holds its
  actions on the library's word for its own scan but draws "Scanning…" only
  from its own reads, which do not take that word up. Move… and Remove from
  this library say why through O250's words; Scan directory and Remove…
  say nothing of the directory's own scan. It is on `main` too. *Closed
  2026-11-16 by the first scan's progress and Cancel, whose bullet for it
  follows O313's, below.*
- **O258 — a directory's removal answered just before its library's rename
  loses its report. Open.** With the directory's page open beside its
  library's, both answers taken before the screen draws again, the
  removal's first, leave the person on the renamed library's page for the
  removed directory, which says it has no directory at this address, and
  the report is gone: the rename still reads the page as the directory's,
  since the removal's change of page is not drawn yet. Read, not run, and
  on `main` too; the other order is tested.
- **O259 — a first scan's end draws "Never" for a moment. Open.** As a
  scan a library's page watched ends, its Last scan cells draw what the
  list said before the scan until the list read the end sends answers. The
  drive saw it once, "Never" between "Scanning…" and a first scan's time,
  with the column's width held (O253). It is on `main` too (read, not run).
  *The page described here is `main`'s: since the first scan's progress
  and Cancel (2026-11-16) the library page takes `scanning` from the scan
  feed, and this was not checked against it.*
- **O260 — Scan library is not held while a scan around one of the
  library's directories runs. Open.** Remove… beside it is held then, in
  O250's words. A press is answered 202, and its scan waits for the job
  lock while the page draws it as scanning. The drive saw the button free
  beside the held Remove… and did not press it. The press's answer and
  its wait are read, not run, and the same on `main`, where the held
  Remove… says nothing.
  Whether to hold it is a decision, not made here. *The page described
  here is `main`'s: since the first scan's progress and Cancel (2026-11-16)
  the library page draws its scans from the scan feed and its Scan library
  reads Cancel while a job holds the library, and this was not checked
  against it.*
- **O261 — the jsdom project's log carries 49 stderr blocks from files
  this PR did not touch. Open.** Forty-eight are `savePrefs` warnings,
  where `localStorage` reads as undefined, beside Node's warning that no
  `--localstorage-file` was given, and one is a React Router warning in
  `Series.test.tsx`. Every test passes. It is on `main` too (read, not
  run).

**The pre-deploy survey of 2026-11-10** read the formats a deployed store
keeps, before the first real data exists, and opened O262, O263 and O264.
Lane 1 of the pre-deploy spec
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-pre-deploy-design.md`, §2) closed them,
and O185, an older row that had no bullet; their bullets follow.

- **O262 — a work's slug drops letters outside ASCII and keeps runs of
  dashes and the archive's extension. Closed.** A work's slug and the
  edition key an edition-of proposal's accept writes now follow one rule (a
  rule's own edition key is stored as typed), so a title outside ASCII keeps
  its letters, a slug loses its archive extension, and the series cover's
  redirect encodes what it names. A slug is minted once, so the rule holds for works minted
  from here on, and a dev database keeps its old slugs until it is rebuilt.
  *O282 makes a scanned work's slug from its series and volume and re-makes
  existing slugs once, and O284 drops the archive extension from a title
  made from a file name — see their rows.*
- **O263 — no backup before a migration. Closed.** The open now takes the
  backup the README asked the owner to take by hand, names it for the
  migration, and refuses to migrate without it. `--keep` leaves those
  backups alone, so they are deleted by hand. By the owner's ruling of
  2026-11-11, a migration that fails and is tried again takes no new backup
  while the newest such backup opens at the database's version and the
  database file and its `-wal` are unchanged since it, judged by their
  modification and change times, so a restart loop does not fill the disk.
  A backup is copied under a hidden name and renamed to its own once whole,
  so a copy cut off part way never stands for the database.
  *O269 has since built a fresh database in one transaction, so opens
  racing a new library's first build take no backup and none is refused;
  two processes upgrading an older database in the same second can still
  refuse one. See its entry below.*
- **O264 — three document readers take a newer version, and `hand::save`
  writes over a newer hand document. Closed.** The readers refuse a newer
  document in the sidecar's words, `hand::save` and an in-place export leave
  one as it is and say so, a stamp refuses up front over a newer
  sidecar, sibling or hand document, and the server's alignment correction
  refuses before it writes over a newer sidecar. The notes document now
  declares `taiyaku_notes: 1` (lane 2, O244): the notes `PUT` and
  `library import` refuse a newer one, asking the version before the shape,
  an in-place export keeps one, and a stamp refuses beside one.
  **The stamp also re-keys the hand document**, added to this lane by the
  owner's ruling of 2026-11-10. A stamp moved each member's `sha256` and only
  renamed the hand document, which keys members by those digests, so a
  library rebuilt from the directory dropped hand-set chapters. Now
  `hand::rekey` replaces each stamped member's digest in the file as it
  stands: after `hand::rename_from` moves it to the new key, or where it is
  when the key held. A stamp cut partway, or one that fails after its
  renames, re-keys it where it was for the archives it renamed, and the
  cut's error, like the transaction's, says how many archives were
  rewritten and that a rescan reconciles them. It re-keys an existing document in a
  root that declines documents too, where `rename_from` already moves one.
  `Applied::document_rewritten` and the stamp screen's line say when the
  document at the work's address was re-keyed. Residuals:
  - **The address window.** A library rebuilt from the directory straight
    after a stamp that failed after its renames, with a hub member stamped,
    finds the document still under the old key, and so none at the new
    one, until a rescan of the live library carries it there.
  - **An error after the commit**, `hand::path_for` or `hand::rename_from`
    failing, answers `Err` although the stamp committed. Its message says
    the stamp itself is recorded and that the hand document stays at the
    old key, where the next scan reports it as an orphan; the document is
    re-keyed there, stranded as in O81.
  - A failed re-key is silent on the screen: it shows only as
    `document_rewritten: false`, where a metadata edit says why.
  - A hand document this build does not read, malformed or refused by
    `LibraryDoc::from_json`, keeps its old digests.
  - Any file already at the new key, newer or not, stays untouched. The
    work's own document is re-keyed at the old address, the answer says
    `document_rewritten: false`, and a rebuild reads the file at the new
    key as the work's (O81).
  - `stamp::rewrite_one` failing after its own rename, in its directory
    sync, leaves that archive stamped and its digest out of the re-key.
  - A metadata edit made between a stamp that failed after its renames and
    the rescan saves the rows' old digests over the re-keyed document,
    which then names them until the next save.
  - The re-key leaves the document's `updated` as it was.
  - An imported work's stamp that is cut, or whose `record` fails, returns
    before its in-place export, as on main, so the work's `taiyaku.json` and
    its siblings keep the renamed archives' old digests. Only a stamp and
    `library export` call `export::work`, so a scan does not rewrite them;
    whether a rescan reconciles such a work's rows is not established.
- **O185 — a cut stamp left a staged archive the next scan read. Closed.**
  The stamp now stages under a dot name, which the scan's walk skips, so a
  cut stamp's leftover is hidden from the library rather than read as an
  entry of it. It is still a copy on disk, up to full size, until that
  archive is stamped again, and a leftover under the old name, from before this
  change, is still scanned.

**O265 was opened on 2026-11-11**, when the advisory check had failed on
`main`'s lockfile since its scheduled run of 2026-11-09, and its bullet
follows.

- **O265 — RUSTSEC-2026-0459, a SQLite flaw reported against
  libsqlite3-sys 0.36.0. Closed.** rusqlite 0.43 compiles SQLite 3.54.1
  into the binary through its `bundled` feature, past the fix in 3.54.0,
  the image installs no `libsqlite3-0`, and `deny.toml` no longer ignores
  the advisory. Debian's build carried two settings this code relies on that the bundled one lacks:
  `Library::configure` now turns on `secure_delete`, and the `Dockerfile`'s
  `server` stage keeps the parameter ceiling at 250000, where other builds
  have SQLite's default of 32766. SQLite's security fixes now arrive by
  updating `libsqlite3-sys` in `Cargo.lock`, with a `rusqlite` bump when the
  fix is outside the range `rusqlite` accepts, and `cargo deny` reports an
  advisory against the copy the lockfile holds. Its whole-branch review
  opened O387.

**The whole-branch review of O265's close opened O387**, and its bullet
follows.

- **O387 — a 500 can send the client the SQL statement that failed to prepare.
  Open.** rusqlite 0.43's error for a prepare SQLite refuses at a position in
  the statement reads as the message, the whole statement and the offset, and
  the routes whose 500 body is the store's error text pass that on: to any
  signed-in account on the library, OPDS, works-list and truth routes, and to
  an administrator on the configuration routes. The one cause found is a
  listing past the build's parameter ceiling, 250000 in the image, which no
  request can bring about on a smaller library. Only a build at the default
  ceiling was seen to answer this way, at 33000 works. A generic 500 body with
  the detail in the server's log clears it, as `routes::answered_and_logged`
  already does for the progress and notes routes.

**Lane 1's reviews** opened O267, from the review of its Finish fix wave, and
O268, from its Task 7 review. Both are on `main` too; their bullets follow.

- **O267 — the alignment correction's 500 named a server path to a reader.
  Closed.** Since O58 only an administrator corrects an alignment, so the
  500 keeps its path as an administrator's route. A sweep of the reader
  routes found that a page, a thumbnail, OPDS's page and cover, a download,
  and a position or notes save that the store cannot make could each send a
  path too;
  each now sends a sentence naming what could not be read, or that the
  library could not answer, and writes the full error to the server's log.
  `two_waiting_saves_each_wait_only_for_the_lock` (O272) asserts that
  sentence now, and "database is locked" is in the log alone. The work
  document's member paths, which the sweep's shape does not reach, are
  O280.
- **O268 — an in-place export keeps a notes or progress file only another
  reader holds state for, and says this library never read it. Open.**
  `migrate::absorbed_for` answers `false` for a per-user document whose
  state is all another account's, so the export keeps the file, and the
  CLI's kept line says "this library has never read it", which is wrong
  there. The "note: N other reader(s)…" line beside it says part of it, and
  `export::work`'s "What an export will not touch" does not list the shape.

**O269 was opened and closed on 2026-11-11**, when
`several_first_opens_of_one_fresh_library_at_once_all_succeed` failed in a
pre-deploy lane's run, and its bullet follows.

- **O269 — an open racing a fresh database's first build backed it up, and
  one of three or more could be refused. Closed.** O263's backup asks for
  the version before any lock, and a fresh database was built one committed
  migration at a time, so an open that arrived after the first commit read
  it as an older database: it backed up a part-built empty store under a
  `-before-v19` name, and a second such open in the same second found the
  first's copy still being taken and refused to start. A fresh database is
  now built in one transaction, chosen by the version read under its write
  lock, so other opens see version 0 or the finished schema, take no backup,
  and wait for the lock instead of building again; a fresh database whose
  build fails stays at version 0.
  `schema::tests::opens_arriving_while_another_builds_a_fresh_database_all_succeed_and_take_no_backup`
  holds a real open part-way through the build while three more arrive, and
  `schema::tests::a_fresh_database_whose_second_migration_fails_stays_at_version_zero`
  pins the rollback; both failed on `main`. An older database keeps a
  transaction per migration, so O263's residuals for it stay: two processes
  upgrading one database in the same second can refuse one, and an open racing
  an upgrade can back up a part-migrated database.

**The pre-deploy missing-works PR 1 of 2026-11-11**, the first of lane 4's
two PRs (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-pre-deploy-design.md`, §5),
closed O48 and narrowed O91; their bullets follow.

- **O48 — a scan that read part of a directory was applied silently.
  Closed.** It is still applied, and no threshold is chosen: the derive
  after it marks missing, and so hides, each work none of whose files a
  directory it was under still holds, by an entry of its digest or any
  entry at its path that the walk did not find empty, and the scan report
  and the CLI count them. A scan that finds the files again brings back the same works, with
  their positions and notes.
- **O91 — a work whose files went stood listed for good. Narrowed.** Every
  derive marks such a work missing; it is left out of every listing a
  reader browses, `/api/works` and OPDS; the reader and its own OPDS feed
  answer it 404 with the reason; and a scan that finds one of its files
  again where it was clears the mark on the same work. A directory holds a
  member where it has an entry of its digest or any entry at its path that
  the walk did not find empty, whatever its digest (the user's ruling of
  2026-11-11, "Path counts too"), so a missing work has nothing to read at
  its path, and no copy of its bytes, in any directory it was under; a
  folder volume emptied in place, its folder left, reads missing (one
  emptied within the same second as the change its last walk read can
  leave unmoved the size and mtime the walk compares, and then keeps its
  digest and reads present until a walk finds its mtime moved, the walk's
  skip already filed as O56). A work
  whose file a nested directory took over, and whose name gives that
  directory's rules no series, reads present, and stays so when the file is replaced in place
  there: it keeps its member's digest and page count, and the reader opens
  the new file at its path up to that count. A member's file that goes
  between a walk and the derive leaves its work present until the next
  walk; the scan report names it among the files gone before they could be
  hashed only where its entry had no digest yet, as for a file the walk
  found new or changed since its last hash. A directory's or library's
  removal no longer deletes a work whose file lies inside a directory left, unless it reads that file as
  vanished, by the user's rulings of 2026-11-10 (overlapping-libraries
  decision 21): a member whose row goes with it is shown, and one with no
  row copied goes to the nearest directory left around its file and stays
  missing until that directory's walk records the file. Where that
  directory's patterns keep its walk off the file, the member is outside its
  grant (the user's ruling of 2026-11-11, "Narrow the grant"): its accounts
  are answered as for a slug no work holds, and an administrator, or an
  account whose grant reaches the member through a directory holding it or
  whose walk reaches its file, still addresses it. A file with no row has
  vanished only where every walk that may last have looked for it reaches it
  (the removed directory's own, and that of each directory nested in it
  whose tree holds the file; a directory around the removed one is not
  asked), where the disk, asked before the removal's transaction, holds
  nothing at its path, and where each directory whose tree holds the file
  reads present and holds a name a walk visits, §8.1's test for an unmounted
  share (the user's rulings of 2026-11-11, "Fix it" and "Add a guard"). A
  pattern edit (`config_api::patch_root`) runs no scan, so a lifted pattern
  makes a walk reach a file it never looked for, and the disk keeps that
  file's work. Nothing removes a missing work on request until the second
  PR. Left as found, from this PR's reviews:
  - A file a nested directory's patterns exclude stays with the directory
    around it where that directory's walk reaches it, and no walk reads it
    again while the nested directory exists: deleted from disk, its work is
    never marked and stays listed, as on `main`.
  - A pattern the outer directory adds over a file it holds for a nested
    directory takes effect at the nested directory's next scan. One the
    outer directory lifts does not bring back a file the nested directory
    excludes; lifting the nested directory's pattern and scanning it does,
    as does removing it and scanning the outer directory.
  - In a store a `main` build since #226 scanned, with a nested directory
    whose patterns covered files, those files' rows were dropped at the
    hand-over or when the nested directory came to exclude them. The first
    derive with this PR marks their works missing though the files are on
    disk, until the nested directory lifts its pattern and scans, or,
    read and not run, is removed and the outer directory scans, where the
    outer's walk reaches the file.
  - Until a scan's derive has hashed them, the entries a store carried over
    from `main` holds at its members' paths with no digest are hashed by
    the first rule preview or save or removal, which reads those files
    inside its write transaction, and again by each preview or rehearsal
    rolled back. One scan after the deploy, before rules are edited, hashes
    them once outside any transaction.
  - At a removal, a member with no row whose file the nearest directory
    left excludes stays missing even where a directory further out admits
    the file, since no walk reads under a directory what its patterns
    exclude. It comes back when that directory lifts its pattern and scans,
    or is removed and the walk around it reaches the file.
  - A file gone from disk inside a directory left is kept, missing, by a
    removal wherever one of the walks that may last have looked for it
    excludes it, the removed directory's own or that of a directory nested
    in it, scanned or not, or wherever a directory whose tree holds it
    reads absent or empty. The second PR is to remove such a work on
    request.
  - A share mounted below a directory, at a path that is none of the
    directories, is not asked whether it is mounted. While it is unmounted, a
    removal reads a file with no row under it as gone where every walk
    that may last have looked for it reaches it, as after a pattern lifted
    with no scan since, and deletes its work, positions and notes; the
    dialog counts them first.
  - The grant asks a directory's patterns about a member with no row there
    both as a file and as a directory, since a member records no kind,
    where the walk asks each name once, as what it is. So a pattern naming
    only directories (ending in `/`), such as `*.cbz/` over an archive or
    `Series/*` with `!Series/Series - v01/` over the folder it names, can
    keep such a member outside the grant of a directory whose walk reaches
    its file. Until that directory's next scan records the file, an account
    whose grant reaches the member only through that directory is answered
    as for a slug no work holds, where the walk's answer would show it the
    work or say its files are missing; the work's positions and notes are
    kept, out of that account's reach.

**O271 was opened on 2026-11-11** by the review of that PR's removal count.
It is on `main` too, and its bullet follows.

- **O271 — a removal's answer counts 0 for what its first derive pass
  changed, its marks apart. Open.** A real removal that takes a directory
  derives inside its transaction, then again after the commit, and answers
  the second pass, which finds the first's changes made and counts none.
  Where a hand-back rekeys a work, the dry run answers `rekeyed` 1 and the
  removal 0, for a directory and a library alike; by reading, `raised` and
  the fold counts read 0 the same way. The administrator sees the dialog's
  figures, then the report after the removal, and `RemoveRoot.tsx` hands
  the real answer on so that a `lost_positions` reaches someone, while that
  is one of the counts the second pass zeroes. `scan::with_marks_of` adds the first
  pass's `marked_missing` and `found_again`; the other counts are not
  fixed.

**Lane 2's review of its Finish fix wave** opened O270, and its bullet
follows.

- **O270 — a derive between a stamp and the next scan of the stamped
  archive's directory puts the old digest back. Closed.** The stamp writes
  each new digest to the archive's `scan_entry` as well as to its member,
  found by its path relative to the member's root, never by digest, since
  two copies under one directory share one. A derive before the next scan
  of that directory reads the new digest there and leaves it on the member,
  and a position or note written in that window is anchored on the new
  digest and stays so after the scan. *Closed 2026-11-17 by the
  paused-directory freeze, whose paragraph follows O340's bullet, below.*

**Lane 3 of the pre-deploy spec**, scheduled scans
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-10-pre-deploy-design.md`, §4), closed O186
and narrowed O51 on 2026-11-12, opened and closed O266, from its derive
lease's review, opened and narrowed O272, from its fix waves' review, and
opened O273, from its first drive, and O274, from its second; their bullets
follow.

- **O186 — a scan cut during its derive read `ok`. Closed.** The server's
  scan job marks `deriving` each directory whose walk wrote `ok`, until its
  derive ends, and `serve` rewrites a `deriving` left by a stop to
  `interrupted` before it binds, so the status reads `interrupted` until the
  directory's next scan.
  A derive that waits for another's reads `waiting`, as does a scan that
  waits for the server's job lock, and the start rewrites a `waiting` a stop
  left to `interrupted` too.
  The startup scan walks every directory that is not Off and that no scan
  already holds *(and, since the first scan's progress and Cancel of
  2026-11-16, that no Cancel paused: O313)*; an Off one keeps `interrupted`
  until it is next scanned.
  The CLI's `library scan` writes no `deriving`, so a CLI scan cut during
  its derive still reads `ok`, and the next derive heals it, whichever scan
  runs it, since every derive covers the whole store.
- **O51 — nothing scheduled a scan. Narrowed.** Each directory has a
  schedule of its own, shared by every library that holds it: Automatic, at
  the unwatched interval; Every, at least 5 minutes, which the server
  enforces; or Off. The directory's page saves a choice at once, and Every
  saves the last Every interval the page has read or saved, at least 5
  minutes, or 24 hours where there is none. A server with a live registry
  scans every directory that is not Off at startup, and then each due
  directory, as one job per tick *(passing over, since the first scan's
  progress and Cancel of 2026-11-16, a directory a Cancel paused: O313)*. A scan accepted while another scan or library job in the server runs
  reads `waiting` until it holds the job lock, then what its last scan left
  until its walk records. The add no longer writes the probe's interval.
  The watcher, and the probe kept at startup, wait for the NAS measurement.
- **O51 — two derives at once.** Every whole-store derive holds a lease on
  `<store>.derive-lock`, SQLite's own lock on a file beside the store, which
  the kernel drops with its process. The server's scan job and the CLI's
  `library scan` wait for it; a rule save, a preview, a removal and a stamp
  try it once and answer 409 in the job lock's words. A server scan that
  waits for the lease reads `waiting`, then `deriving`, but for a walk it
  refused, which keeps `refused`. A library's scan status and
  `GET /api/library/derive` say whether a derive holds it. The pages hold what the lease refuses, Save and
  a stamp's confirm also what the job lock refuses, say why, and read again
  until it is free; a directory's page adds `· waiting` to its Scanning…
  line while its scan waits *(since the first scan's progress and Cancel of
  2026-11-16 it draws the scan feed's step line instead, which reads
  "Waiting for another job" while the scan waits: O312)*.
- **O266 — a cookie request answered 401 while another connection held the
  store's write lock. Closed.** The session lookup's sweep, which ran on
  every request, failed it when it could not take the write lock within the
  busy timeout, and the reader looked signed out. The lookup now refuses an
  expired session in its read, and the sweep and the slide are best effort.
- **O272 — a request's write waits for a derive's, holding the shared
  connection. Narrowed.** A cookie request's slide of its session or sweep
  of a stale one, an API-key request's touch of its key, and a Basic
  request's clear of its failures are each tried once without waiting for
  the store's write lock, and dropped where another connection, such as a
  derive, holds it, so "last seen" and "last used" lag only while one does.
  A Basic request with no failures to clear writes nothing. A page turn's
  progress save, a note's save, and a truth or alignment save each write
  through a connection of their own, opened for that save, so each waits for
  the lock on its own, up to the busy timeout, behind no read and no other
  save but the note or truth saves already under way on the same work, by
  any account, and a correction its document refuses, such as one with a
  stale `If-Match`, answers before it waits. One account's progress saves on
  a work land in the order they reached its handler, after authentication:
  one that gets the lock after a later one has been written writes nothing,
  and an older save on another edition leaves that edition at its earlier
  slot. One account's save can wait for another's commit to finish its WAL
  checkpoint, a wait bounded by one checkpoint. What remains: such a
  save still waits while a derive holds the lock, up to 5 s, and a note or
  truth save queued on its work up to 5 s more for each save ahead of it,
  and fails where its wait ends; and a wrong Basic password's two failure
  records, the pair's and the address's, a login, a logout, and a key,
  session or password change still wait on the shared connection, with
  every other request behind them, as does a queued server scan's
  write-back of its directories' last words where its own connection
  cannot be opened; where that write fails, the directory reads `waiting`
  until its next scan or the next start. A wrong password for an account
  that exists writes a third record, its account's count (O279), tried once
  without waiting. A derive writes nothing for a work, series title, proposal or missing-work
  mark it would leave as it stands, reading each first and taking no write
  transaction for one.
- **O273 — an open page does not see a scan it did not start. Closed.** A
  directory's page and a library's page read the facts when drawn and after
  their own actions, and poll only while a scan they know of runs or
  something holds them, so after a scheduled scan Last scan keeps its old
  time and "next scan" a time already past until a reload. Main's pages do
  the same after a CLI
  `library scan`; scheduled scans make it routine. The drive's record is
  `.superpowers/sdd/pre-deploy-evidence/lane-3-scans/drive1.md` (not
  committed), Observations. *Closed 2026-11-16 by the first scan's progress
  and Cancel, whose bullet for it follows O257's, below.*
- **O274 — at 1280 px an open volume's panels sat in their tile's column.
  Closed.** The compact series tiles of 2026-11-14, whose bullets are
  below, lay an open volume's panel over the rows below its tile, two
  tiles and the gap wide, or the page area's width where that is less, and
  where the account may edit it holds the whole editor, the stamp section
  included where it may also stamp, in `button` and `on-select` mode
  alike. The phone fixes had narrowed it on 2026-11-13 to
  its 1280 px half by fixing the 390 px one, a long path in a stamp plan
  taking the Series page sideways on a phone: the plan draws each path
  through `PathWithBreaks`, and the roots of the alignment panel, the
  metadata editor and the stamp section take `overflow-wrap: anywhere`,
  which they still do in the panel. So at 390 px a plan's paths, the
  title, an alignment error, a stamped content_key and a save's unwritten
  reason wrap inside the panel, in either column, and none of them scrolls
  the page sideways. The 1280 px column, about 130 px wide, was where the
  2026-09-18 settlement (style-pass §7 ②) kept the panels, which made
  moving them the owner's decision; O283 was that decision. As filed, a
  long scratch path widened the page to 459 px at 390 px; the drive's
  record is `.superpowers/sdd/pre-deploy-evidence/lane-3-scans/drive2.md`
  (not committed), Observations O-a and O-b.

**Lane 1 of the go-public spec**, Add as Off and the README
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-go-public-design.md`, §3), closed O275
and O276 on 2026-11-12; their bullets follow.

- **O275 — an added directory was scanned before it could be set. Closed.**
  Both add forms draw "Don’t scan yet (schedule Off)", unticked as each
  opens. A ticked add of a directory no other library holds writes its
  schedule as Off in the add's own `INSERT`, so it waits for a Scan press,
  and its edition key and patterns can be set first; it stays Off after
  that press. Both add routes take `scan_interval_secs` and refuse what the
  directory's `PATCH` refuses, in its words. A directory another library
  already holds keeps the schedule it shares, and where that is not the
  one the add asked for, the line that says it is also another library's
  names it. A directory that is Off and never scanned reads "Never · until
  Scan is pressed" in its library page's Last scan, except while a pressed
  scan waits for the job lock or the page draws it running.
- **O276 — the README's proxy lines, restores, compose block and silence
  about an add's scan. Closed.** The proxy example under "Using it" sets
  `$http_host`. Both restores move the `-wal` and `-shm` aside with the
  database and give the restored file the server's owner, and the
  roll-back recreates the container on the pinned image. The compose block
  carries the WUD labels, and the setup text says when a directory added
  on Configuration → Libraries is first scanned, and how to add one Off.

**Lane 2 of the go-public spec**, server hardening
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-go-public-design.md`, §4), closed O277,
O278 and O279 on 2026-11-12; their bullets follow.

- **O277 — the server sent no security headers. Closed.** Every answer now
  carries `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Content-Type-Options`,
  `Referrer-Policy` and `X-Frame-Options`, set by one layer over the whole
  router. The policy lets a page run scripts only from its own origin and
  denies framing. The theme script that runs before first paint moved into
  `web/public/theme.js`, so the policy allows no inline script. HSTS is
  left to the proxy, where TLS ends.
- **O278 — the login limiter keyed an IPv6 client by its whole address.
  Closed.** Every limiter key now holds an IPv6 client as its /64, after
  reading an IPv4-mapped address as its plain form, so a client cannot
  rotate through its /64 for fresh counters, and mapped IPv4 clients do
  not share one key. The session row still records the whole address.
- **O279 — nothing counted one account's wrong passwords across
  addresses. Closed.** A wrong password for an account that exists, at the
  login route or over Basic, is counted against the account by its id,
  from whatever address; an unknown name, or a wrong current password at
  the password change, counts against none. The thirtieth in a 15-minute
  window prints one warning to stderr, and the Users screen marks the
  account until the window lapses. Nothing is locked: the pair lockout is
  unchanged.

**Go-public lane 3 of 2026-11-12**
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-go-public-design.md`, §5) closed O58, and
O241 with it, O267, O184 and O248, and opened O280 from its plan's second
spec gap. O58 and O184 had no bullet; theirs follow, with O280's.

- **O58 — a key could rewrite the shared truth and alignment documents.
  Closed.** Both writes open with the administrator's gate, so only an
  administrator, by a browser session or the account's password, never a key,
  writes either, and a key still reads both; the web offers correcting and
  labelling to an administrator alone. The write halves of the
  overlapping-libraries design's decision 8 are kept, unreachable
  (the go-public design's §5, decision 6), and the tests
  that drove a limited account through them are void:
  `routes::tests::narrowing`'s
  `a_truth_write_manga_read_before_it_was_granted_kids_is_refused`,
  `manga_alones_truth_write_keeps_raws_entry`,
  `a_truth_write_changing_raw_as_manga_alone_is_refused`,
  `a_correction_naming_a_side_kids_does_not_see_is_refused_before_its_body`,
  `manga_alone_corrects_en_to_fr_with_its_own_documents_etag`,
  `correcting_raw_and_en_as_manga_alone_is_refused` and
  `correcting_a_side_the_view_hides_is_refused_as_a_hidden_work`;
  `routes::tests::a_hidden_work_is_refused_before_its_correction_is_read`;
  and `auth::tests`'
  `patch_alignments_refuses_a_correction_naming_a_withheld_edition`,
  `a_restricted_readers_own_etag_round_trips_through_a_correction_between_visible_editions`,
  `a_correction_between_visible_editions_omits_the_withheld_one_from_its_response`
  and
  `a_correction_naming_the_withheld_edition_on_the_from_side_is_still_refused`.
  Tests that sent such a write beside another subject drop it or expect the
  gate's 403. Three unit tests call `truth::as_stored` directly and hold its
  narrowed path; O58's and O191's rows name them.
- **O184 — a write within one refresh of a work's deletion brought it back.
  Closed.** A live registry never mints a `bridge:` row: a progress, notes
  or truth save, or a correction not already true, to a work whose row is
  gone answers 404, and a correction then writes neither the file nor a row.
  A fixed registry still mints, for `taiyaku-serve`'s fixtures and its `corpus.rs`.
- **O280 — the work document sends each member's server path. Closed.**
  An administrator signed in by browser or by password is sent the work
  document with each member's stored path. Anyone else, an administrator's
  API key included, is sent each member's file name in its place, with an
  `ETag` over what it is sent. The stored document, its format on disk and
  the correction are unchanged, and the reader, which reads only a path's
  last part, needed no change.

**O280 and housekeeping, 2026-11-12**, closed O280 on the owner's rulings
of that day, and opened and closed O281, found by go-public lane 1's drive;
O280's bullet is above and O281's follows. It also corrected the
`taiyaku-serve` row's caching sentence, which said the four routes whose
bytes a member's `sha256` fixes are kept fresh for a day; it now says what
each of them sends.

- **O281 — a fast burst into New library's directory path dropped a
  keystroke. Closed.** The directory picker told New library of each change
  from an effect, a commit after the change, and New library set state from
  it, so each keystroke committed twice, and a burst of input events ran
  past React's nested-update limit, its error #185. The picker now tells its
  caller in the same handler as each change, and not on mount. jsdom throws
  the error but keeps every character, so the burst test holds the error;
  the dropped keystroke was seen in a real browser, by go-public lane 1's
  drive.

**Go-public lane 4 of 2026-11-13**
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-12-go-public-design.md`, §6) closed O240
and O244; their bullets are with the overlapping-libraries PR 1's, above.

**The phone fixes of 2026-11-13**
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-13-phone-fixes-design.md`) closed O141,
O171, O172 and O229, and narrowed O274 to its 1280 px half; O274's bullet
is with lane 3's, above, and the four closes' follow.

- **O141 — on a phone the readout line ran past its row. Closed.** The
  text sits in a span inside the row now, and the span ends it in "…"
  inside the row's padding; the row keeps its one line and its 32 px. Text
  that fits reads as before, whole and centred.
- **O171 — iOS zoomed the reader when the note editor's text box took
  focus. Closed.** A coarse-pointer rule of its own in `reader.css` gives
  the docked panels' text fields the reader's 16 px floor, and the text box
  no longer carries the inline font that beat any stylesheet rule. Under a
  mouse it stays 14 px.
- **O172 — the note editor named a slot counting from 0. Closed.** Its
  heading, each review row's slot and the slot a row's note travels to in
  the edition viewed now count from 1, as the readout does; what is stored
  is unchanged.
- **O229 — the reader's account panel opened only from the keyboard.
  Closed.** Settings' head row has an Account… button, before Close, and
  a press on it closes Settings and opens the account panel, so a tap
  reaches the panel from a book. When the panel closes, focus goes back
  where closing Settings would have put it: to ⚙ when ⚙ opened Settings,
  to the page when a key pressed on the page did. Shift+A over Settings
  now does the same; before this branch it opened the account panel with
  Settings left up and drawn over it, two modals at once, found by reading
  the code. The owner chose the Settings entry and ruled Shift+A over
  Settings in, both on 2026-11-13.

**Shorter book URLs of 2026-11-14**
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-14-shorter-urls-design.md`) closed O282,
which had no bullet, and opened and closed O284; their bullets follow.

- **O282 — a book's URL carried a slug made from its title. Closed.**
  A scanned book's slug is its series' name and its volume, `berserk-v01`,
  minted once its row holds both; a book without a series or a volume takes
  the slug its title gives, as a work newly imported from a `taiyaku.json`
  does. Migration 23 re-makes existing slugs once, a `bridge:` placeholder's
  apart, and an old slug is not redirected.
- **O284 — a title made from a file name kept the archive's extension.
  Closed.** Such a title, and one the store imports from a `taiyaku.json`,
  drops one trailing archive extension when anything is left, and migration
  23 drops it once from
  each stored derived title that has more than the extension, a `bridge:`
  placeholder's apart; a title typed by hand shows as typed.

**The compact series tiles of 2026-11-14**
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-14-compact-series-tiles-design.md`) closed
O274 and O283, and their whole-branch review opened O287; O274's bullet is
with lane 3's, above. The owner's asks of the same day opened O285 and
O286. The other four bullets follow.

- **O283 — a volume's tile kept its buttons on a line under its title, and
  its panel pushed the rows below it down. Closed.** A tile is its cover
  and its title. `i` sits on the cover's bottom-right corner, outside the
  tile's link; where every pointer can hover it shows only while its tile
  is hovered or holds focus or its panel is open, by opacity, so Tab still
  reaches it, and where any pointer is coarse it is always shown. ⇄ takes
  the cover's top-right in the Series grid; the library grid's and the
  table's are unchanged. In `button` mode ↓ is ↓ Download, a 14 px word
  button at the panel's foot. Where a tile has no `i`, with `panel` set to
  `off` or `on-select`, ↓ takes `i`'s corner, size and hover rule, and an
  on-select panel draws none.
  The panel lies 4 px under its tile, over the rows below, so no tile
  moves as it opens or closes: two tiles and the gap wide, or the page
  area's width where that is less, from the tile's left edge, or back from
  its right edge where rightward would pass the page area's end, and laid
  again as the tile's width changes. It is drawn as View's panel is, above
  the covers and their marks and under the phone bar and View, and holds,
  12 px apart, the Title field where the account may edit, its stamp
  section where it may also stamp, the alignment detail, drawn bare, and
  ↓ Download where a download is allowed.
  The Title field wraps its whole title at rest as while it is edited, as
  tall as the title up to five lines and then scrolling, and never grows
  or moves when clicked. It saves as it is left or on Enter, and at the
  end of its label's line says "Saving…" once a save has been out 200 ms,
  until no save is out, and "Saved" as the last lands, for 3 s or until
  the next edit, so a save that lands sooner shows only "Saved"; Save and
  the paragraph repeating the server's title are gone. An
  unchanged title is not sent, and a blank one is put back and not sent.
  Escape puts back the stored title, the one mounted or the last a save
  stored, or while a save is out the one being sent, and withdraws a save
  asked for meanwhile. A title left, entered or asked for by a close while
  a save is out is sent once that save lands, if it still differs, so one
  save is out at a time and the newest text goes last; one typed and not
  yet left waits for the next leave, Enter or close. After a failed save
  nothing queued is sent, and the failure stays under the field until the
  next save is sent, the panel closes, or the field is back at the stored
  title: put back by an Escape in the field, or found there by a leave, an
  Enter or a close, left blank and put back or typed back by hand, which
  sends nothing. A field that still has focus is being edited again, so an
  Escape there puts back the stored title. Neither that Escape nor a leave
  or an Enter back at the stored title takes away the note that a save
  landed but was not written beside the library, which speaks of the
  stored title.
  The panel closes on Escape, a press outside its tile and panel, `i` again,
  and in `button` mode focus arriving outside; in `on-select` mode focus on
  another tile moves the panel instead, a pointer leaving the tile closes
  nothing, and a pointer entering another tile moves no panel while focus is
  inside one, nor while the open field holds a title whose save failed.
  Every close, and every move to another tile's panel, first asks the editor
  to save a changed title, again after each save that lands, and goes ahead
  once nothing is left to send; a save that fails keeps the panel open with
  the failure shown, and one stored but not written beside the library keeps
  it open once, with the unwritten reason shown. An Escape in the Title
  field while it is edited puts its title back, and the next closes the
  panel and sends focus back to `i`, or in `on-select` mode to the tile's
  link, its corner ↓ or an unreadable volume's box, without opening the
  panel again; `i` again closes it with focus on `i`. Either close moves
  focus only if it is still where it was when the close was asked for, or in
  the panel, or on the page's body, so focus moved elsewhere while a close
  waited on a save stays there. Escape is caught on the way down at the
  document and stopped, so the phone drawer stays open; while a panel is
  open it takes every Escape on the page but the Title field's own while it
  is edited and one that ends an input method's composition, and where View
  is open too one Escape closes both. A press whose target is the page area
  itself (`main`) or the document's root closes nothing, so the scrollbar
  reaches ↓ Download with the panel kept; anywhere else outside the tile
  and its panel, the gap between tiles included, a press closes it.
  While it draws the grid the Series page keeps its scrollbar's gutter,
  `main`'s from 900 px up and the document's below, so a panel run past
  the page's end brings no scrollbar that would move every tile, and that
  panel ends the page with as much room below it as the last row has:
  `main`'s block-end padding, and below 900 px the bottom safe-area inset
  as well.
  **What it reopened and reversed.** The 2026-09-18 settlement that a
  volume's panels fit inside its tile (style-pass §7 ②), which the phone
  fixes kept as a non-goal, is reopened by this, the owner's own ask; both
  specs carry a dated pointer to the compact series tiles' spec. The
  owner's Title box ruling of 2026-11-13 (phone fixes, "The Title box
  opens downward") is reversed: the field wraps at rest, never opens, has
  no Save, and saves as it is left; Enter still saves.
  Download §8 (`2026-08-23-library-download-design.md`)
  gave each volume tile one control and the panel none, since a download
  in a panel some readers switch off is one they lose. ↓ Download now sits
  in the `button` panel, and ↓ takes `i`'s corner wherever a tile has no
  `i`, so every mode still has one download per tile; §8 carries no
  pointer, and this bullet records the reversal.
- **O285 — a cover-size slider in place of `density`. Closed.** The owner
  asked on 2026-11-14 for a slider that sets the covers' size in place of
  `density`'s two steps, `comfortable` and `compact`. Compact sets
  `.library.compact .grid` and `.volumes` to `minmax(6.5rem, 1fr)` columns
  and a 0.6rem gap, against `.volumes`' 7.5rem and 1rem, and a second
  `.library.compact` rule sets a panel two tiles and that gap wide until
  `tilePanel.ts` lays it. Left out of the compact series tiles by their
  spec's Non-goals; not built. *Closed 2026-11-15 by the cover-size slider
  and the Continue row, whose bullet for it follows O300's, below.*
- **O286 — the reader strip's scrollbar, "like click and move". Closed.**
  The owner asked on 2026-11-14 to "make the scroll bar for the filmstrip
  usable to scroll … like click and move". Read here as the mark on the
  progress line under the strip, which shows how far along its travel the
  rail stands (O216), taking a press and a move to scroll the strip, as a
  scrollbar's thumb would; the rail itself already takes a mouse's drag
  (O216). That reading is not yet confirmed with the owner, and a drawn
  scrollbar instead would reverse O138's ruling of 2026-10-11, by which
  the rail draws no scrollbar and the wheel scrolls it. Open questions:
  whether a press on the line away from the mark jumps there; how the drag
  works on the line mirrored for a work read right to left; and touch. Not
  built. *Closed 2026-11-15 by the strip's progress line as a scrollbar,
  whose bullet for it follows O287's, below.*
- **O287 — a close while a stamp request is out drops its outcome. Open.**
  Found by this branch's whole-branch review, and deferred. A close of the
  panel, or its move to another tile, waits only on the Title field's save.
  A plan read or a stamp still out then answers to an editor that has gone
  with the panel, and nothing aborts it, so its plan, "Rewrote N archives."
  or its failure is shown nowhere. `main` dropped it the same way when `i`
  again or a move to another tile closed the editor, and the closes this
  branch added, Escape, a press outside and, in `button` mode, focus
  arriving outside, drop it too. Whether a close waits on a stamp request,
  or this is accepted, is not decided.

**The strip's progress line as a scrollbar of 2026-11-15**
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-14-strip-scrollbar-design.md`) closed
O286, and what its drive found about a focused tile was filed as O289 at
the owner's ask the same day; their bullets follow.

- **O286 — the reader strip's scrollbar, "like click and move". Closed.**
  The progress line under the strip is a scrollbar for a mouse, as the
  owner settled it over six rounds of a prototype. A press on the mark and
  a move drag the strip, the mark staying under the pointer where it was
  taken; a press on the line away from the mark centres the mark on the
  pointer and goes on as a drag. Past either end the strip stops at the
  end, nothing glides after the release, and a press stops a glide the
  rail is running. Only a mouse is answered; a finger and a pen swipe the
  strip on its tiles as before. The mark is as wide as the share of the
  volume the strip shows, held between 64 and 160 px. Only a 10 px band
  centred on the line takes a press, drawn wherever some pointer is fine, a
  touch laptop's trackpad included, and a mouse's press there turns no page,
  selects nothing and moves no focus itself. Any mouse move over the
  reader while the bars are up wakes the line a little thicker, with nothing
  else in the bar moving, and it sleeps a second after the last move, except
  while the pointer rests within 16 px above or below the line or a press
  holds it. The line, its fill and the mark grow and shrink as one, eased,
  and not eased with the reader's animation off or under reduced motion. The
  fill's leading end is round. The Title field's failure text is drawn in
  `--danger`, as the reader's and the account's failures are.
  **What it replaced and gave back.** O216's width rule, an eighth of the
  share on show and never under 32 px, is replaced, and O216's spec §3,
  which left a drag of the mark and a jump on the line out of that PR, is
  overtaken; O216's row, its notes section and its spec carry a dated
  pointer. O138's ruling stands, and the rail draws no scrollbar; what the
  ruling said it cost, a mouse's fast way across a long volume, is given
  back on the line, and its row says so.
  **What the plan settled beyond the prototype**
  (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-14-strip-scrollbar.md`, its gaps). The
  wake asks the band's condition, `(any-pointer: fine)`, where the
  prototype also asked `(hover: hover)` for it, so the band never takes a
  press on a line that cannot wake (gap 1). A press on the band where the
  mark was hidden moved focus and could start a selection; every primary
  mouse press on the band is now prevented, mark or none (gap 4). The bars
  hiding during a hold left the hold standing, so the line, once the bars
  came back, stayed awake until a press on it, or a move over it with no
  button down, ended the hold; the hold now ends as a release would, and the
  line comes back at rest (gap 6). The prototype's one sample of the mark
  4.4 px off a dragged pointer was a read taken between a write and the
  next frame, never painted; but a jump did paint the mark off the pointer
  for a frame, and `placeMark` now writes the mark where the pointer puts
  it while a hold is on (gap 7). `docs/notes.md`, "O286", has the
  readings, and what the band costs where it is drawn: over its top 4 px
  the wheel and a pen's press no longer reach the rail, and in Chromium a
  finger's tap on the band is moved onto the tile above it.
- **O289 — a focused strip tile loses its focus to a far jump or a long
  wheel scroll. Open.** Found by O286's drive and filed at the owner's
  ask. On the 237-page volume, in Chromium and Firefox and in both reading
  directions, a tile holding focus lost it to `body` when a far jump on
  the progress line, or a long wheel scroll over the tiles, carried the
  strip far from it: the strip's window takes a tile that far out of view
  off the page. On the 7-page volume the tile kept it, and with focus on
  the page itself a jump kept it. Whether it predates O286 rests on
  reading, not on a run on `main`. `docs/notes.md`, "O286", has the
  readings.

**The books PR of 2026-11-15** (#249, EPUB books and the fixes its review
asked for) opened O290 to O295 and O299 from that review, O296 to O298
from a test drive of it, and O300 from the review of its fix round; their
bullets follow.

- **O290 — a rule capturing `title` makes two comics one work. Open.**
  Every entry with no volume is grouped by the title a rule captured for
  it (`Alone::Titled`), comics as well as books, so a user's regex rule
  capturing `title` over `Oneshots/Ghost Story [a].cbz` and `[b].cbz`
  makes one work whose edition holds both files, its pages running on
  from one to the other. Before the books PR they were two works. No
  seeded rule captures `title`.
- **O291 — the notes `PUT` stores a run that marks no text. Open.** A
  note's run of text is checked only for a start at or before its end, so
  an empty run, or one past its block's text, is stored. Drawing clamps
  it, and the web client builds a run only from a selection, so only
  another client can send one.
- **O292 — a book's cover is its first image by name. Open.** A book
  edition's cover comes from its page 0, which for an EPUB is the first
  image entry by name, not the cover its OPF declares. An EPUB of text
  alone has no cover: the request is a logged 404, and the tile falls back
  to the title placeholder.
- **O293 — an edit made while a merged notes write is out is lost.
  Open.** When a book's notes write comes back merged with another
  device's, the undo history starts again at the merge, rightly, since an
  undo past it would write the other device's notes away. An edit made
  while that write was out is replaced by the merged notes, with no way
  back.
- **O294 — an EPUB of pictures alone cannot be read. Open.** A
  reflowable EPUB holding only images, a comic converted by Calibre say,
  has no text blocks. Since the review's fixes the scan report names it
  under "Pages could not be counted" and the Libraries page counts it;
  reading it as a comic is what is left.
- **O295 — a download's type followed its file's name. Closed by RAR
  PR 2.** A download passed through takes its type and extension from the
  format the scan stored for the file, where the file is as that scan saw
  it, and otherwise from a sniff of the file (`download::sent_as`). So a
  comic archive named `.epub` downloads as a `.cbz`, and the feed's link
  for a reflowable EPUB named `.zip` is typed `application/epub+zip`, as
  the route sends it. Only bytes no signature matches are typed by their
  name.
- **O296 — making translations one work is done by hand. Open.** It
  takes a folder layout (`Author/Title (Translator)/file.epub`), a regex
  rule capturing the same title from each folder, and a prefix rule per
  translation's folder setting its key and language. `library rules
  --import` replaces the whole set, so adding one rule from the CLI is an
  export, a hand edit and an import; nothing in the UI suggests any of it,
  and a derive run before the rules leaves separate works that keep their
  first titles.
- **O297 — an edition is labelled by its key, and its language is the
  rules'. Open.** An edition is labelled by its raw key (`es`, `ormsby`),
  and its language comes from the rules unless a person sets it, not the
  EPUB's own `dc:language`.
- **O298 — a restart aligns each book again, and a pin fetches the whole
  book. Open.** Alignments are kept in memory only, so every restart
  aligns a book again on its first open; and a pin makes the reader fetch
  the whole book again, every edition's text, though only the links
  changed.
- **O299 — loose ends in the books code. Closed.** The book reader takes
  a tap by the page reader's `TAP_SLOP`, and its other figures say why
  they are what they are, or that they were chosen by hand;
  `LengthScorer::refit` is gone, its one measurement having scored worse;
  the experiment reports, through `Band::holds`, the key links a band
  would cut, none of 821 at ±400; and a pair of straight `"` is one
  quotation, as a curly pair is.
- **O300 — a book's hub file going after a translation was titled apart
  strands the rest. Open.** With `en` the hub of `en`, `ja` and `ko`, a
  rule titling `ja` apart into a work of its own leaves an edition naming
  its file on the book's row. Once `en`'s file goes, `derive::held_work`
  refuses `ko` the book's row, since a file of the row is held by the
  other work, and mints a new one, so the reader's position, notes and
  pins stay on the old row, as before the fallback existed. A right
  answer needs each volume-less hub member's work as it stood before the
  derive, read once per derive beside `placed`. The case to rebuild is
  `a_part_titled_apart_before_the_hub_file_goes_leaves_the_rest_on_the_books_row`.
  A second case, older than the books PR, is the same function's
  numbered-volume branch, which takes the row at the volume's address with
  no key check: once a volume's hub file goes and the edition left holds
  the bytes of another work's hub, a derive writes the volume onto that
  work and counts it `rekeyed` (`derive::write_work`), and moves the
  volume's hand document to that work's address where it has none
  (`hand::rename_from`).

**The cover-size slider and the Continue row of 2026-11-15**
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-14-cover-size-and-continue-row-design.md`)
closed O285, opened and closed O288 for the owner's asks about the
Continue row, and opened O301 for what its last review found about the
row's place on a window resize; their bullets follow.

- **O285 — a cover-size slider in place of `density`. Closed.** View's
  Density switch is a Cover size slider, in the home page's View and a
  series page's alike, and covers are its size wherever they are listed:
  the library grid, the Continue row and a series page's volumes. It runs
  from 96 to 240 px with the default, 144 px, at the middle of the track
  over a small mark; the left half moves 1 px a step and the right half
  2 px, an arrow key moves one step, and a double-click anywhere on it
  resets it to 144 px and saves, with no catch at the middle. Each step of
  a drag is saved as it is drawn. From 900 px up the covers are exactly
  the size, as many as fit at the least gap with the spare room spread
  into the gaps, and a short last row keeps the same columns; below
  900 px they fill the row, as many as fit at the least gap and each grown
  to an equal share, so the slider sets the least a cover may be *(except,
  since O302, where the list is narrower than one cover; its bullet is
  below)*. The least gap narrows under the default size. A stored
  `compact` becomes 104 px and `comfortable` 144 px, and the next save
  stores the size in place of `density`.
  View's words cannot be selected, and a press anywhere on a checkbox's
  row, from the panel's edge to edge, toggles it once, a press on its
  words that moves a few pixels included, which Firefox's label alone
  would drop (`ViewMenu.tsx`'s `sendRowClick`).
  **The slider is a kind of setting**, at the owner's ruling of
  2026-11-15: a module declares that a number preference is a slider, with
  its scale, and the generated panels draw it, View and the reader's
  Settings alike, so C1 §4's "a browse module needs no settings UI of its
  own" holds whole and no panel names a key. A declared slider's default
  must be its middle position, where the mark is drawn, and building the
  registry refuses one that is not.
  **What it changed elsewhere.** A cover asks for an image by the width it
  is drawn at, or on a phone by a bound on it, where O133 had it ask by
  screen density alone; O133's row carries a dated sentence. The specs
  that described Density or a fixed cover width as current (C1 §4, the
  sidebar and readability redesign's §2, the style pass's §7.2 and the
  compact series tiles'), and the loading work's where it describes the
  covers' `srcSet`, carry a dated pointer, their prose kept. `docs/notes.md`,
  "O285 and O288", has what the build found beyond the prototype and the
  reasons the comments no longer give.
- **O288 — the Continue row lined up with the sidebar and the grid.
  Closed.** Opened and closed here, for the owner's asks of 2026-11-14 and
  2026-11-15. From 900 px up the Continue heading's hairline is drawn
  level with the sidebar's Libraries heading's, under a fine pointer and,
  in Chromium, a coarse one, and nothing above the heading moves. The row's covers are
  the grid's width and sit over the grid's columns, from 900 px up at the
  grid's spread gap and below it at the grid's filled column width, also
  once more volumes are in progress than fit and the row scrolls. A side the
  row can still scroll to fades to the page, a card under the fade still
  takes a press, and a card's focus ring lifts the fade. A hairline under
  the row sets it apart from the library below, drawn only while the row
  is. O132, reading progress on the Continue cards, is not built here; the
  owner asked on 2026-11-14 to take it up as a quick follow-up, and its
  row says so. A cover-size change keeps the row's place: a row scrolled
  to its end stays at its end, and otherwise the card at its start edge
  stays there as far as the row reaches; a row too short at the new size
  to bring that card to its start edge stops at its end. A window resize
  keeps the place the same way (O301, below). One edge is left as it is, in
  `docs/notes.md`, "O285 and O288": where a browser draws the row's own
  scrollbar, it fades at its ends with the row.
- **O301 — the Continue row's place was not kept across a window resize.
  Closed.** A window resize keeps the row's place as a cover-size change
  does: a row scrolled to its end stays at its end, and otherwise the card
  at its start edge stays there, the same fraction past its edge, as far
  as the row reaches. It holds for any change in the list's width, a phone
  turning and the sidebar coming and going at 900 px among them, and a
  window drag neither creeps nor loses a place near the row's end. A
  change in the number of volumes in progress drops a kept place, so the
  next size change or resize starts from where the row was last seen. A
  row that fits never counts as at its end, and the offset into the start
  card is scaled to the new pitch; both have tests now. Its row has the
  detail.

**The Continue row across a resize of 2026-11-16**
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-15-continue-row-resize-design.md`) closed
O301, and opened and closed O302 on the owner's ruling, for the question
the cover-size slider's notes had left for the owner; O301's
bullet is above and O302's follows.

- **O302 — below 900 px a list narrower than one cover overflowed
  sideways. Closed.** Below 900 px a cover is never wider than its list:
  where the list is narrower than one cover, on the home grid or a series
  page, the one column takes the list's width, and the Continue row's
  cards take it too. Everywhere else the slider still sets the least a
  cover may be. Before, a column was never narrower than the slider's
  size, so 240 px covers in a very narrow window, or in a browser zoomed
  in until it was that narrow, spilled past the list sideways.

**The first scan's progress and Cancel of 2026-11-16**
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-15-first-scan-progress-and-cancel-design.md`,
the first of three PRs from the owner's first NAS import) opened and closed
O310 to O313, from that import, closed O257 and O273, opened O314 to O317,
from the same import, for the second and third PRs, opened O318, from its
own review, opened O319, for two parts of O273 the scan feed did not close,
opened O320 and O321, from its whole-branch review, opened O322 and O323,
from its drive, and closed O323 by design on the owner's ruling; their
bullets follow.

- **O310 — a scan's walk read every page's local header. Closed.** A
  `.cbz`'s pages are listed from its central directory alone, through one
  64 KiB buffer, so listing an archive reads the same for four hundred
  pages as for four: under `strace`, listing alone, the test's archives of
  4 and 400 pages took 16 and 1,204 reads before and 5 and 5 after, and
  sniffed and then listed, as a walk does, 10 and 10. Over this machine's NFS
  mount of the share, the walk-only bench's mean per archive was 4,475.33 ms
